surfaces.part: bench front face with gold emblem

answer.evidence: The bench is the main body. Rows 12-20 form a plank-grained top surface that ends in a lighter front-edge line at row 19 (L=130), then row 20 and a dark shadow line at row 21 (L=42). Below it is a 24-row vertical front panel (rows 22-45) with a gold emblem, so the bench has a top and a front face. The three chair backs (rows 0-10, 30 px wide in total) are drawn only as vertical faces with a small lighter cap at rows 2-4. No chair seat is visible, because the bench hides it, so the chairs show no horizontal seat surface. This matters for a 'seat' kind. The bench itself reads as three-quarter view.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a large wood bench front with a gold coin emblem and three dark chairs behind it. It has only 18 distinct colours against 38-40 for the large references (stall, well), and a median of 7 colours per tile against 17-20 for those two. Its 15% flat-fill coverage is above the 0% of the well and hedge and just above the stall's 13%. The big front panel reads as broad mid-brown areas with sparse vertical plank lines and little per-plank grain or highlight. The wood ramp looks like about 4 steps against 5-6 in the stall and well. The chair backs are near-uniform dark blocks with minimal shading. The outline is mixed: 40% of dark edge pixels are neutral, so some edges are dark brown and others are close to black, where the stall and hedge are tinted at 0-1% neutral. The piece is clean and readable, but it is flatter and thinner than the large references.
